title: P0 decisions, lifecycle, status, and recovery journey

declaredIntent.requestedOutcome: Make P0 decisions, status, lifecycle, stop-condition, and recovery guidance understandable and safe for English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese readers.

outOfScope: Installation, first calibration, first Work Item, adoption overview, and security or trust-boundary overview content; these remain successor P0 Work Items.
Full translation of P1/P2 technical references, archived evidence, release notes, plans, or audit documents.
Runtime behavior, Work Item lifecycle implementation, release metadata, version tags, publication, and generated status semantics.
Historical documents under docs/archive/ except generated Work Item archive evidence.

sources.reason: Approved P0 writing contract, navigation rules, decision/lifecycle/recovery sequence, and WI-4 boundary.
Current topic ownership, localized paths, criticality, and migration status.
Merged reader journey and current successor destinations.
Existing canonical decision-state semantics to rewrite and localize.
Existing canonical lifecycle and stop-condition semantics to rewrite and localize.
Existing recovery guidance and ownership boundaries.
Existing status interpretation and human-action guidance.
Canonical project terminology and human decision boundaries.

riskAssessment.reason: This Work Item rewrites safety-relevant decision, stop, lifecycle, and recovery explanations in three languages; a semantic mismatch could encourage unsafe continuation or conceal the human decision boundary.

reasons: P0 decision and stop-condition content is safety-relevant and must pass full repository verification.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly reopened the documentation plan after WI-3 closure; the approved design defines WI-4 scope, sources, acceptance, and verification.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Create complete same-topic English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese P0 pages for decision states, Cockpit status interpretation, Work Item lifecycle and stop conditions, and recovery overview; each begins with the P0 writing contract and progressive disclosure.
Ensure every status and stop condition explains what it means, what the human must decide, what is safe to do next, and when not to continue or guess.
Ensure each localized page has one to three same-language next steps, is reachable from its matching documentation home within two links, and contains no silent English fallback on the WI-4 P0 route.

Update the authority registry so decision-states, lifecycle, and recovery become active only when all three localized siblings and tests are present; preserve planned successor topics and existing active topics.

Add positive and negative structural tests for decision semantics, status/action mapping, stop conditions, locale parity, same-language navigation, registry ownership, and safety invariants; focused documentation checks pass.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A non-technical reader sees a Green, Yellow, Red, or Unknown status and can explain the decision boundary and safe next action in English, Japanese, or Simplified Chinese.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The reader distinguishes proceed, review, investigate, and stop states without guessing from color alone.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run localized P0 structure, semantic invariant, and status-action mapping tests; inspect each locale's stop-condition layer during review.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A Work Item stops during preflight, verification, merge, or closure and the reader follows the correct recovery owner without bypassing governance.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The reader identifies why execution stopped, what evidence is missing or contradictory, and which human decision or recovery route is required.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run lifecycle/recovery route tests and review same-language next steps for no-guessing and external-responsibility invariants.

guidelines: Use the P0 writing contract: purpose, audience, outcome, scenario, explanation, action/decision, stop conditions, next steps, then technical depth.
Keep Green, Yellow, Red, and Unknown semantics equivalent across locales; never translate away stop, investigation, or human-decision requirements.
Do not claim full multilingual coverage for P0 topics that remain planned outside this Work Item.
Use one canonical owner per topic and keep reference pages as explicit specialist routes.
Do not modify runtime behavior, release metadata, or historical documentation.

intent.problem: The core journey now explains purpose, philosophy, architecture, and boundaries, but readers still cannot reliably interpret a stop, status color, human decision, lifecycle stage, or recovery route in their language. This leaves the most safety-relevant part of understanding as a fragmented technical reference.
constraints: Complete only the decisions, status, lifecycle, and recovery P0 topics assigned to WI-4; installation, calibration, first Work Item, adoption, and security remain successor Work Items.
Preserve native governance semantics and external responsibility boundaries; do not invent runtime behavior or claim provider evidence.
Japanese and Simplified Chinese must be semantically equivalent to English for stop conditions, human decisions, and safe next actions.
Do not change runtime behavior, release metadata, version tags, or historical documentation.
intent.rationale: A reader who understands the project but cannot interpret a stop or recovery state still faces the exact unsafe improvisation the documentation should prevent. A single trilingual journey makes human control and recovery actionable.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: Set only when a human explicitly approves restricted governance paths.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
